title: She Sat on the Idols and Called It Survival
paragraphs:
She Sat on the Idols and Called It Survival
The Hidden Sin We Protect… and the Grace That Still Finds Us There
Nobody talks about what Rachel did next.

We remember the romance.
We remember the beauty.
We remember that she was loved.

But we don’t sit long enough in the moment where she chose to hide something…
not just from her father…
but from God.

The story doesn’t whisper.
It confronts.
Genesis 31:34 says:
“Now Rachel had taken the household idols and put them in the camel’s saddle and sat on them…”
The Hebrew doesn’t soften it. It presses deeper.

וְרָחֵל לָקְחָה אֶת־הַתְּרָפִים וַתְּשִׂמֵם בְּכַר הַגָּמָל וַתֵּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם
(Ve’Rachel laqechah et-haTerafim, vatesimem be’khar haGamal, vateshev aleihem)

She took them.
She placed them.
She sat on them.

Not accidentally.
Not unknowingly.
Intentionally.

These weren’t decorations.
They were teraphim — household gods, symbols of control, inheritance, identity, and spiritual compromise.
And Rachel didn’t just steal them…
She concealed them beneath herself.
There is something terrifyingly familiar about that.
Because if we’re honest, we’ve all learned how to sit on our idols.

We don’t display them anymore.
We bury them.
We justify them.
We protect them with silence.
We smile in worship while guarding what God asked us to surrender.

Rachel even used her condition as an excuse.
She told her father:
“Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise before you, for the way of women is upon me.”

And just like that…
the search stopped.
The lie worked.
The idols remained hidden.
And nobody knew.
Except God.
And that’s where the story shifts from history… to confrontation.
Because some of us have perfected this.

We know how to appear surrendered while secretly clinging.
We know how to sit in church, lift our hands, and still hide what owns us.

The addiction no one sees.
The bitterness we justify.
The secret compromise we’ve learned to manage instead of kill.
We don’t remove the idols.
We just sit on them.
And we tell ourselves it’s survival.
But Jesus never called us to survive hidden…
He called us to be free.
In the Greek, Jesus says in John 8:36:

ἐὰν οὖν ὁ Υἱὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλευθερώσῃ, ὄντως ἐλεύθεροι ἔσεσθε
(ean oun ho Huios humas eleutherōsē, ontōs eleutheroi esesthe)
“If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.”

Not partially free.
Not externally free.
Not performatively free.
Indeed.
Which means the freedom Jesus offers doesn’t coexist with hidden idols.
It confronts them.
Destroys them.
Replaces them.
And here’s the part that will sit heavy on your chest if you let it…

Rachel was chosen.
Loved.
Favored.
And still… she hid idols.
This isn’t about “bad people.”
This is about divided hearts.
Even Jacob — the man renamed Israel — was leading a household where idols still existed.
And maybe that’s the part we don’t want to admit:

You can be close to God…
and still be hiding something.

You can be in the story…
and still not be fully surrendered.
But God doesn’t expose to shame.
He exposes to save.
Because the same God who saw Rachel sitting on idols…
is the same God who sent Jesus to sit with sinners.
To reach under the surface.
To confront what we bury.
To call us out of hiding without rejecting us.
Romans 5:8 doesn’t hesitate:
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
The Greek word for “demonstrates” is συνίστησιν (sunistēsin) — meaning to prove, to establish beyond doubt.
God didn’t wait for you to stand up off your idols.
He came while you were still sitting on them.
Let that break something inside you.
Because grace isn’t permission to hide…
It’s an invitation to come out.
And some of you reading this right now…
You felt this.
Not intellectually.
Personally.
There’s something you’ve been sitting on.
Something you’ve been protecting.
Something you don’t want exposed.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
You are not alone here.
There are others reading this with the same tension in their chest.
And this is where healing begins…
Not in pretending.
But in confessing.
James 5:16 says:
“Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed.”
Healing doesn’t grow in hidden places.
It grows in surrendered ones.
And listen closely…
Rachel’s story didn’t end in that moment.
But it leaves us with a question that refuses to go away:
What are you still sitting on?

Because you can’t fully follow Jesus
while secretly protecting what He died to free you from.
Someone in your life is sitting on something they don’t know how to let go of.
Not to expose them… but to invite them into freedom.
You’re going to need this reminder again when the temptation to hide comes back.
And if you feel something awakening in your spirit…
Stay close.
This is what we do here — we don’t perform Christianity, we walk it, wrestle it, live it.
And if you’re serious about going deeper…
There’s more waiting for you.
And for those who choose to stand with this mission…
Not out of pressure…
But out of purpose.
Because glorifying God isn’t passive.
It’s participation.
And sometimes, supporting what spreads the Gospel…
is part of your obedience.
Here’s the truth you won’t forget:
The thing you’re sitting on is the very place Jesus is trying to reach.
